content: Naftifine is an allylamine antifungal agent that is primarily used for the treatment of fungal skin infections, including interdigital tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea cruris (jock itch), and tinea corporis (ringworm), caused by the organism Trichophyton rubrum. It is available as a topical cream under the brand name Naftin®. Indications and Usage Naftifine is FDA-approved for the treatment of fungal infections such as interdigital tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis. The cream is applied topically once daily to the affected area, including a ½-inch margin of healthy surrounding skin, for a duration of two weeks. It is strictly for external use and should not be used in the eyes, orally, or intravaginally. Contraindications There are no known contraindications for the use of Naftifine. Warnings and Precautions If irritation or hypersensitivity occurs during the use of Naftifine cream, treatment should be discontinued immediately. Patients should be advised to contact their healthcare provider if they experience any adverse reactions or worsening of symptoms. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Data: In clinical trials, the most common adverse reaction was pruritus (itching), occurring in at least 1% of patients. Other reported reactions included dry skin, erythema (redness), burning sensations, and skin irritation. These reactions were generally mild in severity. Postmarketing Data: Additional adverse reactions reported after the drug's approval include redness, inflammation, maceration, swelling, blistering, crusting, and serous drainage. Rare systemic effects such as headache, dizziness, leukopenia, and agranulocytosis have also been reported, though their frequency and causal relationship to the drug are uncertain. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: Naftifine is classified as Pregnancy Category B by the FDA. Animal studies have not shown evidence of harm to the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. It should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefit outweighs the potential risk to the fetus. Nursing Mothers: It is unknown whether Naftifine is excreted in human breast milk. Caution is advised when administering the drug to nursing women. Pediatric Use: The safety and efficacy of Naftifine have been established in adolescents aged 12-17 years for the treatment of interdigital tinea pedis and tinea cruris. However, its safety and efficacy in children under 12 years of age have not been established. Geriatric Use: Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger patients. Pharmacokinetics Naftifine penetrates the stratum corneum of the skin in sufficient concentrations to inhibit the growth of dermatophytes. Systemic absorption is minimal, with less than 2% of the applied dose detected in plasma. Naftifine was detected in plasma in some patients up to 28 days after the last application. Nonclinical Toxicology Long-term carcinogenicity studies have not been conducted with Naftifine. Genotoxicity studies, including the Ames assay and in vivo mouse micronucleus assay, showed no evidence of mutagenic or clastogenic potential. Reproductive studies in animals demonstrated no adverse effects on fertility, reproduction, or embryofetal development at doses up to 6.1 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD). Clinical Studies Tinea Cruris: In a randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study, Naftifine cream demonstrated a higher rate of complete cure (clinical and mycological) compared to the vehicle at week 4. Interdigital Tinea Pedis: In another randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study, Naftifine cream showed efficacy in achieving complete cure at week 6, four weeks after the end of treatment. However, efficacy in moccasin-type tinea pedis was not demonstrated. Administration Naftifine cream is for topical use only. Patients should be instructed to apply a thin layer to the affected area and a ½-inch margin of surrounding healthy skin once daily for two weeks. Storage Naftifine cream should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with permissible temperature excursions between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). Brand Names Naftifine is marketed under the brand names Naftin® and Naftin-MP®. Patient Counseling Information Patients should be informed that Naftifine cream is for external use only and should not be applied to the eyes, mouth, or vagina. If irritation or sensitivity occurs, they should discontinue use and consult their healthcare provider.
